source.name: Radiocommunications (Amateur Stations) Class Licence 2023 - Federal Register of Legislation

classes.name: Amateur Advanced (ACMA recognition certificate or recognised qualification, Advanced)
Amateur Standard (ACMA recognition certificate or recognised qualification, Standard)
Amateur Foundation (ACMA recognition certificate or recognised qualification, Foundation)

note: Operation is authorised by the ACMA class licence (which replaced individual amateur apparatus licences from 19 Feb 2024); a person must hold an ACMA recognition certificate or a recognised qualification (Foundation, Standard or Advanced) and use an assigned VK call sign. Power is tiered per qualification: Foundation 10 W PEP (pX) on all its bands; Standard 100 W PEP for J3E/R3E (SSB) or 30 W mean power (pY) otherwise; Advanced 400 W PEP for C3F/J3E/R3E (incl. analogue TV and SSB) or 120 W mean power otherwise (on 2200m/630m the caps are 1 W and 5 W PEP EIRP). Verified September 2026: the Advanced cap remains 400 W PEP - the rumoured/considered rise to 1 kW PEP was NOT made in the current instrument, and the 2025 Licence Conditions (Amateur Licence) Determination only changed apparatus-licence conditions (e.g. removing a 472-479 kHz Timor NDB restriction). Foundation holders are limited to 80/40/15/10m, 2m and 70cm; Standard adds 20m, 6m (50-54 MHz), 23cm, 13cm (2.40-2.45 GHz) and 5.8 GHz; Advanced adds 2200m, 630m, 160m, 30m, 17m, 12m, 2.30-2.302 GHz, 9cm (3.3-3.4 GHz), 3.4 GHz and all higher amateur bands. There is no 60m allocation for any class. Bandwidth restrictions: segments marked ≤ 8 kHz or ≤ 2.1/3 kHz prohibit wider emissions; segments with the PSD cap allow wider emissions only at ≤ 1 W per 100 kHz power spectral density. Additional geographic limits: 3.4-3.6 GHz is excluded in the listed remote Schedule 3 areas, and all operation is prohibited in the Australian Radio Quiet Zone (WA). Repeaters and beacons require separate transmitter licences and are not authorised under this class licence. WIA band plan (wia.org.au) used only as a cross-check; it is consistent with the licence (e.g. 6m split 50-52 secondary / 52-54 primary, no Foundation access, 10 W/100 W PEP for Foundation/Standard).
